sentences.ko: 결혼 생활 유지하는 게 얼마나 힘든지 넌 몰라.
sentences.text: You have no idea what it takes to make a marriage work.

alts.text: Marriage is hard work, trust me.
Making a marriage work requires far more than you realize.

sentences.note: **what it takes to** ~ 는 '~하려면 뭐가 필요한지', 곧 '얼마나 힘든지'라는 뜻이에요. 해 본 사람이 안 해 본 사람에게 말할 때 씁니다. **make a marriage work** 처럼 make ~ work 는 '~를 잘 굴러가게 하다'라는 뜻이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 뭐, 이왕 하기로 한 거 계속 밀고 나가야지.
sentences.text: Well, if I'm going to do this, I better keep going.

alts.text: Might as well keep at it now.
Since I have decided to do this, I had better continue.

sentences.note: **I better** 는 I'd better 를 말로 할 때 줄인 것으로 '~하는 게 좋겠다'는 느낌이에요. **keep going** 은 멈추지 않고 계속한다는 뜻이고, 떨리는 일을 시작해 놓고 스스로 다잡을 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 우리 방금 창고에 있었는데, 진짜 소름 끼치는 남자를 봤어.
sentences.text: We were We were just in the storage area and we saw this really creepy man.

alts.text: Just saw a super creepy guy down in storage.
We have just come from the storage area, where we saw a very unsettling man.

sentences.note: 이야기를 꺼낼 때 쓰는 **this really creepy man** 의 this 는 '이 사람'이 아니라 '어떤'이라는 뜻이에요. 처음 꺼내는 얘기를 생생하게 들려줄 때 씁니다. **creepy** 는 '왠지 소름 끼치는, 꺼림칙한'이라는 뜻이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그러니까 이번엔 내가 무슨 말을 할지 나도 몰라.
sentences.text: So, who knows what I might say this time.

alts.text: No telling what'll come out of my mouth this time.
Therefore, nobody can predict what I might say on this occasion.

sentences.note: **who knows** 는 '누가 알겠어', 곧 아무도 모른다는 뜻이에요. 앞일을 장담하지 못할 때 가볍게 씁니다. 축사나 발표 전에 농담처럼 하기 좋아요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 8 | Friends

sentences.ko: 넌 그냥 해야 할 일을 한 거야.
sentences.text: You just did what you had to do.

alts.text: There was nothing else you could have done; you did what was necessary.

sentences.note: **did what you had to do**는 힘든 결정을 내리고 마음 쓰는 사람을 달랠 때 씁니다. 상대를 탓하지 않고 "어쩔 수 없었잖아"라고 말해 주는 표현입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 불 좀 살짝 어둡게 해 볼까.
sentences.text: Maybe I'll just turn down the lights a little.

alts.text: Let me dim the lights a bit.
Perhaps I will lower the lights slightly.

sentences.note: 불을 줄일 때 **turn down the lights**나 **dim the lights**라고 합니다. 소리를 줄일 때 쓰는 turn down을 불에도 그대로 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그럼 너도 이제 건강 엄청 챙기는 그런 사람 되는 거야?
sentences.text: So, you're going to be one of those healthy, healthy, healthy guys?

alts.text: Oh, so you're a health nut now?
Are you planning to become one of those very health-conscious people?

sentences.note: **one of those** ~ guys는 "흔히 보는 그런 부류"를 살짝 놀리듯 가리킬 때 씁니다. 건강에 집착하는 사람은 **health nut**이라고 부릅니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 너희가 드디어 아이를 갖게 돼서 진짜 기뻐.
sentences.text: I'm just so happy you guys are finally getting a kid.

alts.text: So glad you two are finally having a kid!
It makes me very happy that you are finally having a child.

sentences.note: **getting a kid**는 입양처럼 아이를 맞게 될 때 자연스럽게 씁니다. 직접 낳는 경우에는 보통 **having a kid**라고 합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 저희 못 알아보실 수도 있어요. 부모님이랑 연락 안 한 지 17년 됐거든요.
sentences.text: You may not recognize us because we haven't spoken to your parents in 17 years.

alts.text: Bet you don't remember us — haven't talked to your folks in 17 years.
Perhaps you do not remember us, as we have not been in touch with your parents for seventeen years.

sentences.note: 오랜만에 만난 사람에게 먼저 **You may not recognize us**라고 말하면 어색함이 덜합니다. 편하게 말할 때는 부모님을 **folks**라고도 부릅니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends
